# Verdant Engine

> Universal 3D browser and WebAssembly game engine in Rust (`crates/verdant-tensor`, `crates/verdant-core`, `crates/verdant-wasm`, `crates/verdant-cli`) mechanized with Prism, unified `uor-matmul` semiring contractions, native WebAssembly `uorc_decompress` + `uor_matmul::codec` zero-decode streaming, Khronos `.glb` scene import and `.glb -> .uorc` transcoding, XPBD articulated joints, 4-wheel raycast vehicles, BVH acoustic occlusion, and 64-frame deterministic rollback.

## Documentation

- [Verdant Engine documentation](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/): Build fast 3D games and interactive worlds for the web and Rust.
- [Build your first 3D world](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/getting-started/): Create a Rust 3D scene, step rigid-body physics, and export a binary asset.
- [Author scenes, physics joints, and spatial audio](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/guides/custom-game-world/): Import GLB scenes, solve articulated joints and vehicles, and mix occluded 3D sound.
- [Stream zero-decode scenes with UORC](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/guides/progressive-uorc-streaming/): Pack and read UORC scene streams step by step in the browser.
- [Verdant Engine API reference](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/reference/engine-api/): Look up crates, modules, rollback types, CLI commands, and 60fps budgets.
- [Unified semiring tensor core and UORC streaming](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/explanation/tensor-and-uorc-streaming/): See how the engine runs exact math and scene streams in any browser.
